summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results comparing Redwood POC setup vs baseline provider. Redwood shows improved p50 latency and comparable p95 after tuning; throughput (QPS) higher with batching and KV cache. Customer raised questions on variability at peak, VPC egress, and quantization impacts. Agreed next steps to run additional long-context and production-sampled tests and share artifacts.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're at 10am PT. quick roll call?
[00:06] Daniel Park: Daniel here, CTO, hi Maya.
[00:08] Sana Ahmed: Sana here.
[00:10] Raj Patel: Raj on infra.
[00:12] Emma Li: Emma, data science.
[00:14] Maya Chen: Great. Luis, want to kick off with the numbers?
[00:17] Luis Ortega: Yeah, thanks. So we ran the baseline runs across the same 2k prompt set you shared, baseline provider (CloudVendorBaseline) numbers we pulled were p50 ~120ms, p95 ~420ms for the 512 token scenario. Our initial Redwood POC default config was p50 ~95ms p95 ~520ms but after the tuning last week (batching window & KV cache warm) we hit p50 ~78ms p95 ~360ms.
[00:40] Sana Ahmed: Wait p95 went down that much?
[00:42] Luis Ortega: Mmhmm, we added aggressive prefix caching for repeated prompt prefixes and tuned the batching thresholds; that reduced tail. There's still a small tail from cold KV misses.
[00:53] Raj Patel: What nodes were those running on? Our baseline is on their managed instance which they advertise as c5/gpu-like.
[00:58] Luis Ortega: For parity we used the customer's requested Gpu-equivalent instance type - 4x A10 equivalent - and we also ran a smaller test on higher mem machines. We'll share the exact instance types in the csv.
[01:10] Emma Li: Throughput QPS? we care about concurrency more than single request latency.
[01:14] Luis Ortega: Right - with continuous batching enabled Redwood sustained ~180 QPS at 512 tokens with 8 concurrent workers, baseline was around 120 QPS under same request mix. At 1k tokens Redwood was ~95 QPS vs baseline ~60 QPS.
[01:29] Daniel Park: That seems promising. Did you include the quantized 4-bit runs we asked about?
[01:34] Luis Ortega: Yes - we ran both fp16 and q4x runs. The q4x runs improved throughput by about 20-25% but added a few ms to p95 in some tails for certain longer prompts - likely due to dequantization overhead in specific kernels.
[01:48] Sana Ahmed: Hmm, tail behavior worries me. Our SLO is p95 < 400ms under normal traffic and p99 under 2x load.
[01:55] Maya Chen: We heard that - part of our playbook is to use hybrid profiles: keep fp16 for critical paths and q4x for background rerank. That keeps p95 tight.
[02:05] Raj Patel: Any memory/eviction issues with the KV cache? we saw evictions in our staging runs.
[02:10] Luis Ortega: We instrumented the KV usage - eviction rate dropped to <2% after we increased cache size and tuned TTLs; the autoscaler also temporarily spills to warm nodes rather than evicting, helps with consistency.
[02:22] Emma Li: Can you share the cache hit rate numbers?
[02:24] Luis Ortega: Yep, we'll include hit-rate graphs; in the tuned run hit-rate avg ~86% during steady-state, cold-starts were lower around 42% but warm quickly.
[02:34] Daniel Park: You mentioned batching windows - any impact to latency variance for small interactive flows?
[02:38] Luis Ortega: We used dynamic batching: short windows (5ms) for interactive routes and longer windows for async; that kept p50 for interactive low. We can make per-route overrides.
[02:49] Sana Ahmed: What about network/VPC egress? our security team flagged concerns about cross-region egress to baseline provider.
[02:55] Priya Nair: To echo, with Redwood Private you can keep control plane in your VPC and route inference in-region; for the POC this was in our hosted POC with regional routing to reduce egress. We can provide architecture doc.
[03:08] Raj Patel: For production we'd want on-prem or VPC mode, yes. Also KMS integration for keys.
[03:12] Priya Nair: Absolutely - we have KMS/HSM integrations and audit-log samples we'll send.
[03:17] Luis Ortega: Back to numbers - we also ran burst scenarios: under sudden 3x traffic Redwood held p95 under 500ms with autoscale rules; baseline saw p95 spike to ~900-1,200ms before shedding.
[03:30] Emma Li: Those bursts are concerning. Did you see any request loss or error rates?
[03:34] Luis Ortega: Error rate stayed under 0.2% for Redwood runs, most errors in baseline were timeouts due to queue saturation.
[03:41] Daniel Park: Can you walk us through the test harness? want to make sure apples-to-apples.
[03:45] Luis Ortega: Sure - harness used JMeter-derived runner that replays traces with original inter-arrival distribution you provided; we matched model version and prompt set. Differences: baseline provider had a different batching strategy we couldn't fully replicate (their managed service groups short/long contexts automatically). We documented those differences in the csv and the script.
[04:03] Sana Ahmed: I noticed the p95 in your initial run was worse before tuning. what changed operationally?
[04:09] Luis Ortega: Mainly three things: increased KV warm-up, tuned batch thresholds, and disabled one fallback path that caused extra serialization. Also bumped thread-pool sizes on the worker which reduced lock contention.
[04:20] Maya Chen: Quick clarification - when you say "baseline" are we talking about their standard managed offering or their new batch-special offering?
[04:27] Luis Ortega: Standard managed offering that Acme currently uses. We can run a comparison to their batch-optimized SKU if you want.
[04:33] Raj Patel: Yes please - that would be good to see.
[04:35] Emma Li: Also could we get per-prompt latencies for the worst 10%? that will help debug tail causes.
[04:41] Luis Ortega: Yep, per-prompt tail dump included.
[04:43] Daniel Park: Any cost delta we should expect? throughput higher but how about $/req?
[04:49] Maya Chen: We ballparked improvement in unit cost of ~15-30% depending on token mix due to batching and cache savings; we'll break that out in the csv with token-level cost.
[04:58] Sana Ahmed: About security docs - send SOC2 and PCI notes if available.
[05:02] Priya Nair: We'll attach SOC2 Type II summary and our security whitepaper and the KMS integration guide.
[05:09] Raj Patel: One more infra question: autoscaler cooldown and cold-starts - we saw 8-12s cold-starts previously.
[05:15] Luis Ortega: With our tuned autoscaler and pre-warm policy cold-starts are ~2-3s for additional replicas because the runtime keeps warm workers in a paused state. We'll show timeline traces.
[05:25] Emma Li: Great. For SLOs - we need p95 < 400ms at nominal load and p99 < 900ms at 2x load; can you target that in the next run?
[05:34] Maya Chen: Yes - action item: we'll aim for that and get back with a targeted run by Friday.
[05:37] Daniel Park: Sounds good.
[05:39] Maya Chen: Quick recap and next steps? Priya, can you capture next steps?
[05:44] Priya Nair: Sure - we'll send: full benchmark csv and script (Luis), SOC2/security pack (Priya), per-prompt tail dumps and per-route configs (Luis), and we'll schedule the on-site latency test if you approve.
[05:58] Sana Ahmed: Approve scheduling after we see the per-prompt dumps.
[06:02] Daniel Park: Ok, thanks everyone.
[06:05] Maya Chen: Thanks - we'll follow up.
[06:08] [call ends]

Notes: occasional transcription errors present - e.g., "dedicate-equivalent" should read "dedicated-equivalent"; references to baseline provider named generically as CloudVendorBaseline. Shared artifacts: link to benchmarks csv (drive link), security pack (internal link), per-prompt tail dump (s3 link).
